description: How green plants make their own food by photosynthesis - a ready-to-present lesson.

slides.heading: Where does a plant's food come from?
bullets: Animals eat plants or other animals for food.
Green plants make their own food - they are called autotrophs.
The process is called photosynthesis.
It mostly happens in the green leaves.
slides.notes: Ask students what a plant 'eats'. Lead them to see that plants do not eat - they build food themselves.

slides.heading: What photosynthesis needs
bullets: Carbon dioxide - taken from air through tiny pores called stomata.
Water - absorbed by roots and carried up to the leaves.
Sunlight - the energy source.
Chlorophyll - the green pigment that traps sunlight.
slides.notes: List the four requirements on the board. Point out that only chlorophyll-containing cells can do this.

slides.heading: The photosynthesis word equation
bullets: Carbon dioxide + Water --(sunlight, chlorophyll)--> Glucose + Oxygen
Glucose is the food; it is stored as starch.
Oxygen is released into the air as a by-product.
slides.notes: Write the equation once, then have the class repeat it aloud together.

slides.heading: The role of the leaf
bullets: Broad, flat shape catches maximum sunlight.
Stomata let carbon dioxide in and oxygen out.
Veins carry water in and food out.
Cells are packed with chloroplasts holding chlorophyll.
slides.notes: If a leaf is available, hold it up and point to the veins and the underside where stomata sit.

slides.heading: Testing a leaf for starch
bullets: Keep a plant in the dark for 2-3 days to remove stored starch.
Expose one leaf to sunlight, cover part of it with black paper.
Boil the leaf in water, then in alcohol to remove green colour.
Add iodine - the lit part turns blue-black, the covered part does not.
slides.notes: This is the classic starch test. Emphasise it shows starch forms only where light reached.

slides.heading: Why photosynthesis matters
bullets: It is the source of almost all food on Earth.
It puts oxygen into the air that we breathe.
It removes carbon dioxide, helping balance the atmosphere.
Fossil fuels are stored energy from ancient photosynthesis.
slides.notes: Connect to daily life: the rice, wheat and vegetables they ate today all trace back to photosynthesis.

slides.heading: Quick recap
bullets: Green plants make food by photosynthesis.
Needs: carbon dioxide, water, sunlight, chlorophyll.
Makes: glucose (food) and oxygen.
Happens mainly in the leaves.
slides.notes: Cold-call four students, one point each, to close the lesson.
